paragraphs.source_en: The basis of all modern discussions of time travel is Einstein's general theory of relativity. As we have seen in earlier chapters, the Einstein equations made space and time dynamic by describing how they were curved and distorted by the matter and energy in the universe. In general relativity someone's personal time as measured by their wristwatch would always increase, just as it did in Newtonian theory or the flat spacetime of special relativity. But there was now the possibility that spacetime could be warped so much that you could go off in a spaceship and come back before you set out (Fig. 5. 1). One way this could happen is if there were wormholes, tubes of spacetime mentioned in Chapter 4 that connect different regions of space and time.
